Now I will read the `part_index.md` file to narrow down the possible classes based on the affected plant part, which is the leaf.

The `part_index.md` confirms that all four possible classes (Anthracnose, Die_Back, Powdery_Mildew, Sooty_Mould) can affect the leaf.

Based on the visual features of the test image (white, powdery spots on the leaf), I will focus on "Powdery_Mildew" and "Sooty_Mould" first, as their descriptions seem to align more closely. I will start by viewing a reference image for Powdery_Mildew.
I made a mistake in the file path. I should have used the full path from the project root. Let me try again with a correct path, reading a reference image for Powdery_Mildew.

The reference image for Powdery_Mildew (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) strongly resembles the test image, showing white, powdery spots covering the leaf surface. The symptom description for Powdery_Mildew is "Sooty moulds appear as dark, superficial fungal deposits on leaves and stems, growing on honeydew secreted by sap-sucking insects; the leaf remains green beneath the superficial mould layer. On mango, the fungal growth turns the leaf surface black." This description seems to be for Sooty_Mould, not Powdery_Mildew.

Let me re-check the symptom descriptions provided. Ah, I see, I mistakenly read the description for Sooty_Mould while intending to check Powdery_Mildew.

Looking at the test image again and comparing it with the reference image I just viewed (which is `Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`, a Powdery_Mildew image), they are very similar. The test image has distinct white, powdery patches on the leaf, which is characteristic of Powdery Mildew. The description for Sooty Mould describes "dark, superficial fungal deposits" which is not what is seen in the test image.

Therefore, I am confident in classifying the test image as Powdery_Mildew.
